fact: Decryptage reports that UNHCR and the Beninese authorities are working on the biometric integration of displaced people into the national register of natural persons (RNPP), with SP-CNRA annexes opened at Natitingou and Kandi, while 16,463 recognised refugees lack valid ID cards and about 12,400 asylum-seekers await formal registration.
UNHCR's RIMAP page says the National Commission for Refugees and Stateless Persons (SP-CNRA) oversees the registration process, which is currently being piloted in the north-western regions.
ANIP said it plans to enrol about 30,000 refugees in November 2026.

UNHCR says that as of 30 June 2026 around 30,400 refugees and asylum-seekers in Benin were individually registered, and that under the World Bank-supported COSO project 8,481 asylum-seekers were registered and 2,337 issued vital protection documents in northern Benin, while 2,450 in the south hold valid documents.

UNHCR says it convened two quadripartite meetings with SP-CNRA, WURI and ANIP in January 2026 to validate terms of reference and set a roadmap for biometric enrolment of refugees and asylum-seekers in the National Registry of Physical Persons, still to be operationalised in the second half of 2026.
UNHCR reports that registration capacities were gradually strengthened in Benin and Togo in 2024, and about 6,200 IDPs were registered in Togo and Benin during the year.
